knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian Determinant of a Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}5 u + 2 v \\ 3 u + v\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=5 u + 2 v$ and $y(u,v)=3 u + v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=5&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=2\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=3&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}5&2\\3&1\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(5\right)\cdot\left(1\right)-\left(2\right)\cdot\left(3\right)\\&=5-6\\&=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}6 u - 3 v \\ \ln{\left(u + v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=6 u - 3 v$ and $y(u,v)=\ln{\left(u + v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=6&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=-3\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=\frac{1}{u + v}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=\frac{1}{u + v}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}6&-3\\\frac{1}{u + v}&\frac{1}{u + v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(6\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{u + v}\right)-\left(-3\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{u + v}\right)\\&=\frac{9}{u + v}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}5 u \cos{\left(v \right)} \\ 2 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=5 u \cos{\left(v \right)}$ and $y(u,v)=2 u \sin{\left(v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=5 \cos{\left(v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- 5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=2 \sin{\left(v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=2 u \cos{\left(v \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}5 \cos{\left(v \right)}&- 5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\\2 \sin{\left(v \right)}&2 u \cos{\left(v \right)}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(5 \cos{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(2 u \cos{\left(v \right)}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(- 5 u \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(2 \sin{\left(v \right)}\right)\\&=10 u\left(\cos^2 v+\sin^2 v\right)\\&=10 u.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}5 u^{2} - 2 v^{2} \\ 5 u^{2} + 2 v^{2}\end{bmatrix}.

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}\cos{\left(v \right)} \tan{\left(\frac{u}{3} \right)} \\ \sin{\left(v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=\cos{\left(v \right)} \tan{\left(\frac{u}{3} \right)}$ and $y(u,v)=\sin{\left(v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=\frac{\cos{\left(v \right)}}{3 \cos^{2}{\left(\frac{u}{3} \right)}}\\\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- \sin{\left(v \right)} \tan{\left(\frac{u}{3} \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=0\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=\cos{\left(v \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\cos{\left(v \right)}}{3 \cos^{2}{\left(\frac{u}{3} \right)}}&- \sin{\left(v \right)} \tan{\left(\frac{u}{3} \right)}\\0&\cos{\left(v \right)}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\frac{\cos^{2}{\left(v \right)}}{3 \cos^{2}{\left(\frac{u}{3} \right)}}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix}\longrightarrow\begin{bmatrix}3 \left(u + v\right)^{2} \\ \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{3}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=3 \left(u + v\right)^{2}$ and $y=\left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{3}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=6 u + 6 v\\\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=6 u + 6 v\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=6 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=- 6 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}6 u + 6 v&6 u + 6 v\\6 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}&- 6 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(6 u + 6 v\right)\cdot\left(- 6 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(6 u + 6 v\right)\cdot\left(6 \left(2 u - 2 v\right)^{2}\right)\\&=\left(- 288 u - 288 v\right) \left(u - v\right)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix})=\begin{bmatrix}\cos{\left(u + v \right)} \\ 6 u + 3 v\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=\cos{\left(u + v \right)}$ and $y=6 u + 3 v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=6&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}&- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\\6&3\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(3\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(- \sin{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(6\right)\\&=3 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix})=\begin{bmatrix}e^{5 u + 2 v} \\ \ln{\left(u v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=e^{5 u + 2 v}$ and $y(u,v)=\ln{\left(u v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=5 e^{5 u + 2 v}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=2 e^{5 u + 2 v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=\frac{1}{u}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=\frac{1}{v}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}5 e^{5 u + 2 v}&2 e^{5 u + 2 v}\\\frac{1}{u}&\frac{1}{v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(5 e^{5 u + 2 v}\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{v}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(2 e^{5 u + 2 v}\right)\cdot\left(\frac{1}{u}\right)\\&=\frac{5 e^{5 u + 2 v}}{v}-\frac{2 e^{5 u + 2 v}}{u}\\&=\frac{\left(5 u - 2 v\right) e^{5 u + 2 v}}{u v}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}e^{u + v}&e^{u + v}\\10 u&4 v\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(e^{u + v}\right)\cdot\left(4 v\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(e^{u + v}\right)\cdot\left(10 u\right)\\&=\left(- 10 u + 4 v\right) e^{u + v}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix})=\begin{bmatrix}\ln{\left(5 u + 2 v \right)} \\ u v\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=\ln{\left(5 u + 2 v \right)}$ and $y=u v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=\frac{5}{5 u + 2 v}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=\frac{2}{5 u + 2 v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=v&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=u\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{5}{5 u + 2 v}&\frac{2}{5 u + 2 v}\\v&u\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(\frac{5}{5 u + 2 v}\right)\cdot\left(u\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(\frac{2}{5 u + 2 v}\right)\cdot\left(v\right)\\&=\frac{5 u - 2 v}{5 u + 2 v}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix})=\begin{bmatrix}5 u \ln{\left(v \right)} \\ 2 u^{2} v^{2}\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=5 u \ln{\left(v \right)}$ and $y=2 u^{2} v^{2}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=5 \ln{\left(v \right)}&\quad \frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=\frac{5 u}{v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=4 u v^{2}&\quad \frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=4 u^{2} v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}5 \ln{\left(v \right)}&\frac{5 u}{v}\\4 u v^{2}&4 u^{2} v\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(5 \ln{\left(v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(4 u^{2} v\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(\frac{5 u}{v}\right)\cdot\left(4 u v^{2}\right)\\&=20 u^{2} v \left(\ln{\left(v \right)} - 1\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T(\begin{bmatrix}u \\ v\end{bmatrix})=\begin{bmatrix}5 \sin{\left(u + v \right)} \\ 2 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}\end{bmatrix}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}\to\begin{bmatrix}x(u,v)\\y(u,v)\end{bmatrix},
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}$, is given by

$$
\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}.
$$

Here, we have $x=5 \sin{\left(u + v \right)}$ and $y=2 \cos{\left(u - v \right)}.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&=5 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}\\\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}&=5 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&=- 2 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}&=2 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y)}{\partial(u,v)}&=\begin{vmatrix}\frac{\partial x}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial x}{\partial v}\\\frac{\partial y}{\partial u}&\frac{\partial y}{\partial v}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\begin{vmatrix}5 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}&5 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}\\- 2 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}&2 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\end{vmatrix}\\&=\left(5 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(2 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\right)\\&\quad{}-\left(5 \cos{\left(u + v \right)}\right)\cdot\left(- 2 \sin{\left(u - v \right)}\right)\\&=20 \sin{\left(u - v \right)} \cos{\left(u + v \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$
